diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The baseline agent fixed the import ModuleNotFoundError by making langchain imports optional, but the build still fails because a pre-existing test failure (test_record_timestamp) involves a timestamp precision issue where init_timestamp == end_timestamp due to time.sleep(0.15) not producing a different millisecond-truncated timestamp in some runs. The agent dismissed this as 'out of scope' but the verifier requires full build success. The relevant skills are around CI analysis and Python testing debugging - these should guide the agent to recognize that all test failures must be addressed, not just dismissed as pre-existing.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill focuses on analyzing CI failures from PR URLs but doesn't guide the agent on how to interpret build-repair tasks where ALL test failures must be resolved for the build to pass. The agent incorrectly concluded a failing test was 'out of scope' when the verifier requires full build success.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add explicit guidance that in build-repair tasks, every test failure counts toward build success - no failure can be dismissed as 'pre-existing' or 'unrelated'. Instruct to re-run full test suite and verify zero failures before concluding. Include heuristics for recognizing when a build is considered passing vs failing (exit codes, test counts, etc.).

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The skill covers writing effective tests but lacks guidance on debugging flaky timestamp/timing-related test failures. The failing test (test_record_timestamp) compares init vs end timestamps truncated to milliseconds; the fix likely requires adjusting timestamp precision in helpers.py (datetime.utcfromtimestamp with timespec='milliseconds') or increasing sleep duration. The skill should help diagnose this pattern.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a section on debugging timing-sensitive tests: when assertions compare timestamps and fail due to equal values, investigate (1) timestamp precision/truncation in the source code, (2) whether sleep duration exceeds the precision window, (3) datetime.utcfromtimestamp deprecation and timezone handling. Include concrete fix patterns like changing timespec from 'milliseconds' to 'microseconds' or using monotonic clocks.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Possibly tangentially relevant since the original build failure involved optional dependencies (langchain extras not installed). The skill could clarify how extras/optional-dependencies work during dependency installation in CI contexts.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add guidance on handling optional dependencies and extras in pyproject.toml: when imports fail due to missing optional deps, options are (a) make imports conditional with try/except ImportError, (b) install the extra, or (c) move the dep to required. Clarify which approach is appropriate for library vs application code.
